title: CRITICAL: capstone dogfood — author a basic Flash game end-to-end and verify in Ruffle
description:
REOPENED by Oracle: partially done — the toolchain proof is real and KEPT (interactivity.spec.ts:697 Dot Catcher: compile -> Ruffle -> click -> pixelDiff 10000, passes; commit 71522ce), but the closure skipped the core acceptance: the game must be AUTHORED THROUGH THE AGENT INTERFACE, not injected as an inline JS fixture via __flashTest.loadDocument(). Remaining scope: (1) author the game by invoking the MCP bridge tools / flash-agent CLI (stage_add_shape, library create/convert symbol, timeline layer+keyframe ops, script_set, publish_swf — see docs/19-agent-interface.md and CLAUDE.md 'Controlling the editor'), either as an e2e spec driving MCP tool calls or a flash-agent script checked into the repo; (2) the game must include the originally specified mechanics: onEnterFrame game loop, Key input, MovieClip.hitTest, score in a TextField, gotoAndStop game-over — the current Dot Catcher (button on(release){nextFrame()}) is a frame-flipper, not a game; (3) publish via the bridge and verify in Ruffle with synthesized input asserting state changes (score increments, game-over reachable). Every gap the bridge has for real authoring becomes a new task. This is the MVP exit criterion; close only with the run command + results pasted here.

--- ORACLE GUIDANCE (mid-flight, do not reset your work) ---
Audit confirms capstone-0519.spec.ts is the right shape: real MCP callTool authoring (doc_set_properties, stage_add_shape, library_convert_to_symbol, stage_update, stage_add_text, timeline_insert_blank_keyframe, script_set, publish_swf) and the AS2 script has all 5 mechanics. The convert-to-symbol registry fix you made (symbol first-frame population) is exactly the kind of bridge gap this task exists to find — commit it. Three things before closing: (1) CURRENT FAILURE: Ruffle renders blank/white (diffVsWhite=0 at spec line ~530) even though publish returns bytes — triage: wait for Ruffle player readiness before screenshotting (see CLAUDE.md visual-oracle learnings), check SetBackgroundColor + first ShowFrame emission, and dump the published SWF bytes to verify definitions precede frame 1. (2) Synthesized input must actually drive the game: the player auto-chases the coin (dx*0.15), so the test passes without ever pressing a key — Key.isDown is in the script but never exercised. Drive movement with page.keyboard (arrow keys) and assert position/score changes attributable to input. (3) Strengthen the final assertion: assert score TextField increments and the gotoAndStop(2) game-over screen is reachable, not just 'pixels changed'. Also: you are working without a lock — acquire one per AGENTS.md.
